questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I chose Australia as a travel destination I have always wanted to go to. Townsville is located right next to the great barrier reef and tropical forests.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: JCU Townsville has an excellent website, but I still don't underestimate the time required to fill out forms.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: Upon arrival, we had an orientation week with a lot of information, including the phone number of a 'tutor' you could text about anything.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: There are many options for off-campus housing. I recommend staying close to campus - you will spend a lot of time here. Make sure you talk to your landlord and have a good feeling about this person, as it is often private persons renting out rooms. Also, having good roomies is essential, so make sure you meet and like them.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Off-campus gives a lot of freedom and is a cheaper option. Having your own personal and quiet space is excellent without a connection to uni-life. However, suppose you only attend one semester (and you love being social). In that case, I recommend staying on campus, as many events happen here - especially in the beginning. This creates an excellent opportunity to make friends very quickly.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: Once accepted by KU, the process was very straightforward. You fill out a few forms and examine which subjects you find interesting. You are thoroughly guided through emails and videos, and I always get swift replies to my emails.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Email mostly, but also beneficial videos on their website.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Registering your classes can be a bit tricky. Coming from FRB. Campus with a straightforward structure, JCU Townsville is very different. Finding fantastic subjects was elementary, but many of these would overlap, making it difficult to make a schedule.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer:
Choosing subjects that don't overlap may be tricky, but it is also okay to show up on campus and ask for help in the first weeks of your exchange. (as well as changing subjects if it wasn't the right fit etc.)
So don't stress too much about it.
Also, exchange is about so much more than attending university, so try not to do too many complex subjects or subjects with many prerequisites.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Things are done differently in Australia (or at least at JCU). So try not to stress too much about it; expectations sometimes seemed very high when it was only to push us to do better.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I did three 2. year subjects and one 3. year subject. Some I found very easy, others were complicated. I also chose topics because I lived in Australia and wanted to learn more about them. Therefore I had many subjects with very little knowledge beforehand.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer:
We had very few on-campus lectures and subjects, with almost only online courses. Also, you hand in assignments throughout the semester that count towards your final grade. This makes the exams less intense and makes the projects more critical. However, I enjoyed this, though there was more stress throughout the semester. 
Also, my exams at JCU were all closed-book, which I find very challenging.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Australian terrestrial diversity
Wildlife Ecology and Management
Australian landscape processes and Evolution
Functional biology of marine organisms

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I enjoyed Australian terrestrial diversity and Wildlife ecology and management. It is the same lecturer hosting these two courses, and he is just a unique and passionate person. These subjects offer a lot of freedom in online recorded lectures with a lot of fieldwork and a field trip. I would not recommend Australian landscape processes and Evolution unless you are really into geology (although this lecturer was also outstanding in teaching). Functional biology of marine organisms, I didn't find fascinating, and many down cuts in previous field trips and excellent laboratory exercises etc., have made this a weighty subject because of the amount of theory.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: I travelled and went diving an unexpected amount of times:) Don't underestimate that you live in a fantastic country with much to offer and see.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Food is expensive, and Townsville housing is cheaper than Copenhagen (especially off-campus).

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: I played a lot of beach volley, I climbed in a centre, and every week an International cafe is hosted. Social sports, where you try various sports, are also highly recommended. Dancing lessons in the city were also a lot of fun. In the first week of orientation, a big market day is hosted, where you meet all the different societies - I highly recommend attending this. I also joined a yoga club which was also very nice. And OF COURSE, you should join the dive club. It has a fantastic community and many significant events and trips.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: If you plan your week right, you might be able to join free BBQs and lunches almost every day:)

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Try to travel around and see Australia. Especially by car is incredible. Also, diving is fantastic.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: The heat during summertime was brutal to adjust to. But the people are very chill, and the food is American/westernised.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer:
Attend every possible International cafe and free lunches etc., on campus. Campus life at JCU is fantastic, and connecting with other exchange students is easy. 
If you are a very social person, I also recommend staying in on-campus accommodation, as this offers further socializing with other students

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Only the heat/humidity is fierce. Otherwise relatively easy to adjust to, I would say.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Talk to the local people. They are all charming, and often you'll get invited to stuff with them.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1. Accommodation: Do you want the VERY social life on-campus or the more chill off-campus? It is easy to find both, but staying off-campus means you can't find a place until you are there to sign and see the room first. 
2. Save up some money. It is nice to say yes to all the possibilities that might come your way.
3. Of course, you should take university seriously, attend classes, etc. But the exchange is about so much more than that. So don't be too afraid of missing out a bit now and then if this means you get to experience something unique.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Take advantage of all the significant initiatives, both on and off campus. You will meet a lot of cool people doing so.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: I was getting to know so many new people around the globe in a tropical country with fantastic wildlife and nature!

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: I struggled to balance my academic life with my social life. But everything turned out more than fine in the end. So don't go too hard on yourself.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
